name: Gabriel Trugillo Jaeger
title: Full-Stack Developer & Network Security Researcher
taglines: Where web development meets network infrastructure
Code that works. Systems that scale. Research that matters.
bio: I'm a full-stack developer from Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, with an unusual background: I've published research on network security while building production web applications. This combination isn't accidental—I believe understanding systems from the user interface down to network protocols makes me a better developer.

about.story:
I build web applications and research network infrastructure—two worlds that rarely meet.

Right now, I'm working at OneWeb Soluções Inteligentes, developing ERP systems that handle real business operations. When I write PHP code to manage inventory or process financial transactions, I'm not building demos—I'm building software that actual companies depend on every day. This work taught me that clean code isn't theoretical. It's the difference between systems that survive and technical debt nightmares.

Before OneWeb, I was a CNPq research fellow at FURG (Federal University of Rio Grande), working on the e-COO project. I built full-stack applications with React, Next.js, and TypeScript while conducting research on network security. That combination—building production apps while researching infrastructure vulnerabilities—shaped how I think about software.

My research focused on BGP routing and prefix hijacking. If that sounds obscure, here's why it matters: BGP is the protocol that holds the internet together, and it's fundamentally vulnerable. I investigated how attackers can redirect internet traffic by exploiting these vulnerabilities. This work resulted in two published papers presented at ERRC 2023 (Regional School of Computer Networks) and earned a Distinguished Work Award at FURG's Scientific Congress.

Most developers build applications assuming the network layer is safe. My research taught me it's not—and that perspective influences every architectural decision I make.

I'm finishing my degree in System Analysis and Development at Anhanguera (2025) while actively studying software architecture. SOLID principles, Design Patterns, Clean Architecture, Domain-Driven Design—I'm not just reading about these. I'm applying them, questioning them, and figuring out when they help and when they're overkill.

What drives me? Building software that's both elegant and resilient. Understanding not just how to make something work, but why it works that way. Thinking in systems, not just features.
interests: Software architecture and design patterns that solve real problems
Network infrastructure and how it affects application design
Building production systems that real businesses depend on
The intersection of theory and practice in software engineering
